pull.title: KAFKA-21286: Share consumer bounds fetch-buffer wait when no partitions are assigned
pull.body:
### Jira
* [KAFKA-21286](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21286): Share consumer may delay fatal startup errors while waiting for the first heartbeat

### Problem
Following KAFKA-19804, the initial heartbeat interval defaults to `request.timeout.ms` (30s) while joining the group to avoid busy-spinning. In `ShareConsumerImpl.pollForFetches()`, the wait duration on `fetchBuffer.awaitNotEmpty(pollTimer)` was calculated solely as `Math.min(applicationEventHandler.maximumTimeToWait(), timer.remainingMs())`.

When a member is joining and has not yet received assignments (`subscriptions.numAssignedPartitions() == 0`), `maximumTimeToWait()` returns the 30-second request timeout. If a fatal error (such as `GROUP_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED`) arrives from the coordinator, the background event handler enqueues an `ErrorEvent`, but the application thread was blocked in `fetchBuffer.awaitNotEmpty` for the full 30 seconds before exiting `pollForFetches()` to process background errors.

### Solution
Align `ShareConsumerImpl` with `AsyncKafkaConsumer` by capping the fetch buffer wait timeout at `retryBackoffMs` when no partitions are assigned (`subscriptions.numAssignedPartitions() == 0`).

1. Added `numAssignedPartitions()` to `AbstractSubscriptionState` and implemented it in `ShareSubscriptionState`.
2. Loaded `retryBackoffMs` from configuration into `ShareConsumerImpl`.
3. In `ShareConsumerImpl.pollForFetches()`, capped `pollTimeout` at `retryBackoffMs` when `subscriptions.numAssignedPartitions() == 0`.
4. Added unit tests in `ShareSubscriptionStateTest` and `ShareConsumerImplTest` to verify that fetch buffer waits and fatal error reporting during startup are bounded by `retryBackoffMs`.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21286: Share consumer bounds fetch-buffer wait when no partitions are assigned

In ShareConsumerImpl.pollForFetches(), the wait duration on the fetch
buffer was determined solely by the minimum of maximumTimeToWait() and
the remaining poll timeout. Following KAFKA-19804, the initial heartbeat
interval defaults to request.timeout.ms (30s) while joining the group.
If a fatal error (such as GROUP_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED) is returned from
the coordinator on the initial heartbeat, the background event handler
enqueues an ErrorEvent, but the application thread was blocked in the
fetch buffer wait for the full 30 seconds before processing background
events.

Align ShareConsumerImpl with AsyncKafkaConsumer by capping the fetch
buffer wait timeout at retryBackoffMs when no partitions are assigned
(subscriptions.numAssignedPartitions() == 0).
